messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1: ALB/ingress errors in euc2 (eastus2). 5xx spike detected on production routes, multiple customers seeing failures. Auto-page to oncall. Please acknowledge.

maria: acked, oncall here. pulling up dashboards.

sven: I'm seeing a surge of 502/504 from the ingress tier around 08:12 UTC. LB error rate + backend latency. adding context: errors mostly on POST /v1/generate and /v1/chat/completions.

alice: any recent deploys?

maria: none in the last 2 hours per deploy bot. looks like connection resets between ALB and envoy pods.

ops-bot: Deploy check: no active deploys in prod-euc2 in last 3 hours.

raj: running quick curl against a few endpoints from a probe host in euc2: `curl -sv https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/health` - encountering TLS handshake reset intermittently.

kevin: digging into ALB target group health: several targets reporting Unhealthy/Timeouts. Could be AZ partial network flap.

maria: running k8s describe on ingress controller pods -> pods look Ready but logs show repeated upstream connection resets. grabbing logs.

maria: ```
# sample from envoy log (truncated)
[2026-03-15T08:12:31Z] "POST /v1/generate" 502 UH/NR upstream reset by peer: upstream_response_timeout
[2026-03-15T08:12:32Z] connection error: RETRYABLE_CONNECT_FAILURE
```

sven: that pattern matches ALB closing connections during TLS rehandshake. can someone run a dig/traceroute to see if Route53 health checks are flapping?

alice: ran `dig api.redwood.example.com @8.8.8.8` - resolving to multiple ALB IPs, but one set of AZ IPs returns higher latency / packet loss. traceroute shows hop 5 -> 7 high loss.

raj: checking cloud provider status for euc2 AZ-B: minor networking incident flagged ~08:05 UTC. linking: https://status.cloud.example/incidents/2321 (internal note).

maria: hypothesis: AZ-B's network path to ALB frontends is degraded causing ALB to drop connections to targets in that AZ, triggering ingress upstream resets and 5xx. impact is cross-region but concentrated on euc2-AZ-B.

kevin: to reduce customer impact we should remove targets in AZ-B from the ALB target group and let traffic redistribute to healthy AZs. planning a quick drain and deregister. any objections?

sven: +1 do it. but watch capacity — we may need to scale Dedicated pools or route to fallback region.

maria: initiating deregister for targets in AZ-B now. command:
```bash
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:targetgroup/prod-api/abcd --targets Id=i-0abc1234,Id=i-0def5678
```
response: `deregistration started`

ops-bot: Alerts: silenced ALB health flapping alert for target-group during mitigation window.

alice: after draining AZ-B targets, 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 2% over 90s. customers reporting partial recovery.

raj: still seeing some DNS TTL edge cases; some clients pinned to IPs in the degraded AZ. suggest we issue a short-lived traffic-shift: update route53 weighted records to favor euc1 region for 5 minutes while propagation happens.

sven: thumbs on that. set weight 90 -> euc1, 10 -> euc2 (remaining AZs).

maria: updated route53 policy. command executed. note: this will cause some requests to land in euc1 where capacity is sufficient.

kevin: raising an incident customer impact note: ~24% of requests in euc2 experienced 5xx at peak for ~7 minutes. Affected customers: partner-x, internal-prod-batch, some free-trial seats. No data loss reported.

maria: continuing to monitor. enabling additional envoy connection pool tuning to reduce resets as a safety measure. applying hotfix config to ingress (1-min rollout):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  envoy_max_conn_age: "30s"
  upstream_idle_timeout: "60s"
```

ops-bot: Config rollout succeeded to 12/12 ingress replicas.

alice: after config and deregistering AZ-B, error rates stabilized under 1% and latency back to normal.

raj: advised support to reach out to the three affected customers with an incident pre-brief and ETA for RCA.

maria: switching to postmortem mode. we'll keep the incident channel open for 1 hour for any late regressions. initial mitigation summary: 1) deregistered targets in AZ-B, 2) route53 weighted shift to euc1, 3) envoy pool tuning.

sven: follow-ups: - verify ALB target health flapping root cause with cloud provider, - evaluate automatic AZ-aware draining on health anomalies, - add synthetic checks hitting IPs to detect pinned clients.

kevin: logging timeline + metrics and will upload to incident doc. tagging @oncall-triage.

incident-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged -> severity reduced to P2 at 08:27 UTC after stabilization.

maria: thanks all. leaving a note: if anyone sees renewed errors, ping here and we'll re-open. :thumbsup:
